A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Skill Expansion and Composition in Parameter Space. Their complete main text, Appendices A–G, equations, figures and tables are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PSEC experiments on DSRL, DeepMind Control Suite, D4RL and Meta-World, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains original PSEC benchmark, ablation and transfer outcomes in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1–8.

M1.justification: The diffusion-policy formulation, LoRA skill expansion and context-aware parameter-space composition remain unchanged, including their objectives and training procedures in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DSRL tasks, DMC standing/walking/running tasks, D4RL dynamics and morphology shifts, and Meta-World continual, few-shot and zero-shot scenarios. Appendix F's additional coverage already exists in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across experiments: the safe-RL baselines in Table 1, Scratch/ASEC/NSEC/PSEC-MLP comparisons, L2M and other continual-learning baselines in Table 3, and dynamics-shift baselines in Table 8 are retained.

E3.justification: The protocols in Section 4 and Appendices C/F are unchanged, including DMC trajectory counts, D4RL source/target sample sizes, Meta-World task splits, training budgets and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Both retain the LoRA-rank and context-awareness ablations, sample and parameter efficiency analyses, t-SNE visualization, trajectory case study and running-policy reward-distribution analysis. Relocated appendix displays do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Seed counts, evaluation episodes and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Examples include 20 episodes and four seeds in Table 1, 10 episodes and five seeds in Table 8, and five-seed standard-deviation bands in Figure 20.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged after matching relocated displays. For example, Table 2 retains PSEC scores of 688, 221 and 247, and Tables 3–7 retain the same Meta-World success rates.

T1.justification: Equations 1–25 and the mathematical assumptions remain unchanged, including the fixed state/action spaces and diffusion, LoRA and composition formulations. No proof, derivation or formal result is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about efficient skill expansion, knowledge reuse, context-aware composition and continual capability growth.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are retained. Appendix A still discusses pretrained-policy coverage, redundant skill-library growth, hyperparameter tuning and the simple composition module, with the same proposed remedies.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Tables 9–11 retain the same implementation details, architectures, LoRA ranks, optimizer settings, batch sizes and training steps. The project-access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B and the bibliography add Cheng et al. (2024a,b), covering world-action model pretraining and RIME, and Ma et al. (2024a,b), covering reward shaping. These four citations supplement existing passages without changing the positioning arguments.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects 'he input feature' to 'the input feature'. Existing 'Xudong et al.' citations become 'Gong et al.', with corresponding author-name corrections in the bibliography. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography and appendix pagination reflow, repositioning existing displays. For example, Table 7 moves from page 31 to 32, Table 9 from page 35 to 34, and Figure 20 from page 34 to 35. Their content and numbering remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds four citations, corrects a typo and citation names, and rearranges existing appendix displays. The method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations are unchanged. These limited editorial and bibliographic edits do not materially strengthen or weaken the paper overall.
